question.text: Will Argentina's Senate give media sanción to a bill suspending or eliminating the PASO primaries in its 26 November 2026 session?
question.resolution_criteria: This question concerns the Argentine Senate session scheduled for Thursday 26 November 2026, planned as the last ordinary session of the 2026 period. It resolves YES if, in a session of the Argentine Senate held on 26 November 2026 (including any continuation of that session past midnight into 27 November 2026), the Senate grants media sanción — final approval by the chamber of origin, sending the bill to the Chamber of Deputies for revision — to a bill that suspends or eliminates the PASO (Primarias Abiertas, Simultáneas y Obligatorias) for all national offices up for election in 2027, whether as a standalone bill or as part of a wider electoral-reform package, and whether the change covers only the 2027 elections or is permanent. It resolves NO if no such approval is completed in that session — including if the Senate rejects the bill, does not bring it to the floor, or does not hold a session — or if the text approved merely makes the primaries optional for political parties or suspends them for only some of the 2027 national offices. Resolution is based on reporting by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) on 26–27 November 2026; the Senate's official session records at https://www.senado.gob.ar/parlamentario/sesiones/busquedaTac can be used to confirm the outcome.
question.fine_print: Approval must be completed in the Senate (both "en general" and "en particular"): a bill approved "en general" whose particular treatment is left unfinished by the end of 27 November 2026 does not count.

research:
Status as of 16 Nov 2026: nothing is settled yet. The bill has no committee report (dictamen), no confirmed floor session and no confirmed 37 votes.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16: I tried to read the Senate session search page (busquedaTac) directly, but it returned an anti-bot captcha, so it shows nothing about a 26 Nov session yet. I could not find an official call for that session. [senado.gob.ar](https://www.senado.gob.ar/parlamentario/sesiones/busquedaTac)
- In practice, resolution will depend on press reports from 26-27 Nov and the Senate's published voting records.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The Asuntos Constitucionales committee meets Tuesday 17 Nov at 15:00. The 26 Nov floor session is planned but has not been formally called.
- The bill has been weakened. Santilli's team now plans a one-time suspension of the PASO for 2027 rather than eliminating them, and it may add "colectoras" (several provincial candidacies attached to one presidential column on the paper ballot) to win over governors. Allied senators say they have not seen the new text. [El Destape](https://www.eldestapeweb.com/politica/gobierno-cede-cambia-reforma-electoral-suspender-paso-antes-2027-20261116050)
- A suspension covering all 2027 national offices would count as YES. A fallback to optional primaries would count as NO.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: Santilli has reportedly told colleagues he has the votes for media sanción. Bullrich still doubts it and says it depends on each senator. Other dates that week:
  - Wednesday 15:00: labor parlamentaria (the meeting that sets the floor agenda).
  - Possible Thursday 19 Nov session on property rights, the disability emergency and the patent treaty.
  - LLA wants a Deputies session on 25 Nov for the 2027 budget.
  
  [El Destape](https://www.eldestapeweb.com/politica/gobierno-cede-cambia-reforma-electoral-suspender-paso-antes-2027-20261116050)
- 2026-11-15: PRO Senate leader Martín Goerling, on the votes: "Yo no lo veo tan certero" ("I don't see it as so certain").
  - He doubts a dictamen on Tuesday if the text changes at the last minute.
  - He called colectoras "un disparate" (nonsense) and suggested splitting the PASO suspension off for later.
  - PRO's executive board, with Macri present, has backed keeping the PASO.
  - Infobae's own count puts real support at about 31-32 votes, short of 37.
  
  [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/politica/2026/11/15/el-pro-cuestiono-la-suspension-de-las-paso-y-puso-en-duda-el-dictamen-si-el-gobierno-modifica-el-proyecto-a-ultimo-momento/); [Ámbito](https://ambito.com/politica/el-pro-volvio-poner-duda-los-votos-del-gobierno-suspender-las-paso-y-cuestiona-los-cambios-las-reglas-electorales-n6345441)
- 2026-11-15: MDZ headline: Santilli is optimistic, while Bullrich repeats that "the votes are not there". [MDZ](https://www.mdzol.com/politica/2026/11/15/fin-de-las-paso-pese-al-optimismo-de-santilli-bullrich-repite-que-los-votos-no-estan-1995490.html)
- 2026-11-14: Noticias Argentinas reports the government has the 10 of 19 committee signatures it needs for the dictamen.
  - On the floor, LLA (21) needs 16 more, roughly 7 of 10 UCR, the 3 PRO and at least 6 provincial senators.
  - The PRO trio (Goerling, Andrea Cristina, María Victoria Huala) were to decide on Monday 16 Nov.
  - Bullrich stepped back from the negotiation.
  
  [Noticias Argentinas](https://noticiasargentinas.com/politica/senado--el-gobierno-ya-tiene-asegurados-los-votos-para-dictaminar-a-favor-de-la-suspension-de-las-paso_a6af72932d33dd5f804808362); [El Ciudadano](https://elciudadanoweb.com/el-gobierno-acelera-en-el-senado-corrio-a-bullrich-y-ya-tiene-votos-para-dictaminar-a-favor-de-suspender-las-paso/)
- 2026-11-14: La Nación, governor by governor:
  - Open to a suspension: UCR governors Cornejo, Pullaro, Sadir, Zdero and Valdés.
  - Aligned with the government: Figueroa (via senator Corroza) and Torres.
  - Hardened their stance and raised demands: Sáenz and Llaryora.
  - Skeptical: Passalacqua.
  - Opposed: Jaldo.
  - Directly opposed: Kicillof, Insfrán, Ziliotto and Quintela.
  
  [La Nación](https://www.lanacion.com.ar/politica/uno-por-uno-como-estan-jugando-los-gobernadores-aliados-en-la-negociacion-con-la-casa-rosada-nid14112026/)
- 2026-11-12: The Senate set the debate date amid the Menem-Bullrich tension. Perfil reports doubts that the votes exist. [La Nación](https://www.lanacion.com.ar/politica/el-senado-fijo-fecha-para-debatir-la-suspension-de-las-paso-en-medio-de-la-tension-con-bullrich-nid12112026/); [Perfil](https://www.perfil.com/politica/senado-el-gobierno-presiona-a-bullrich-para-suspender-las-paso-pero-dudan-de-que-esten-los-votos-necesarios-aU3cY9t0fwE8)

## 4. Base rates
- 2025-02-20: The Senate passed a one-year suspension of the 2025 PASO by 43-20 with 6 abstentions, after Deputies approved it on 6 Feb by 162-55-28. That happened in extraordinary sessions, after the original plan to eliminate the PASO was cut back to a one-year suspension. PRO and part of kirchnerismo voted in favour. [Diario Jornada](https://www.diariojornada.com.ar/388861/politica/el_senado_convirtio_en_ley_la_suspension_de_las_paso); [Chequeado](https://chequeado.com/el-explicador/diputados-debate-la-suspension-de-las-paso-2025-que-son-y-que-dice-el-proyecto-de-ley/)
- So there is a recent precedent for cutting the bill back and then passing it, but it went through in an extraordinary session, not on a fixed November date.
- The current bill has been stalled since May 2026, with only two committee meetings since April. Rushing from dictamen to floor in nine days is a tight timetable.
- The government has said it would move the bill to extraordinary sessions in December if November fails, which makes a slip past 26 Nov an easy option.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question. None of the markets collected by code match: they cover US races and Argentina's 2027 presidential winner (Milei 0.435, Kicillof 0.325).
- Journalists' counts so far: Infobae puts support at about 31-32 votes, against Santilli's claim of 37 or more.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-16 (Mon): The PRO senators were to decide their position.
- 2026-11-17 (Tue) 15:00: Asuntos Constitucionales meets, with the dictamen signing to watch. Goerling doubts it will happen if the text is changed.
- 2026-11-18 (Wed) 15:00: Labor parlamentaria, which could set the agenda for the 19 and 26 Nov sessions.
- 2026-11-19 (Thu): Possible Senate session on other bills.
- About 2026-11-25: Bills put on the floor without a dictamen of at least 7 days need a two-thirds vote, so a dictamen on 17 Nov is close to essential for a simple floor vote on 26 Nov. This is my reading of the Senate rules; I have not verified it.
- Other things that could move the outcome:
  - Whether the final text suspends the PASO for all offices or falls back to optional primaries.
  - Any move to replace Bullrich with Nadia Márquez as bloc leader, which could split the LLA bloc.
  - Demands from Sáenz and Llaryora, and the 2027 budget negotiations running in parallel.
  - A possible decision to move the bill to December extraordinary sessions.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10 days remain. The outcome will be known on 26-27 November 2026. For Yes, a dictamen must be signed (in practice on 17 Nov, so the 7-day rule allows a simple floor vote), the 26 Nov session must actually be called with the bill on the agenda, and at least 37 senators must approve it both en general and en particular. The approved text must suspend or eliminate the PASO for all 2027 national offices, not make them optional.

(b) The status quo is No. The bill has been stalled since May, has no dictamen and no formal session call, and the count is short of 37.

(c) Base rate: when an Argentine government pushes a contested electoral bill with uncertain votes toward the last ordinary session, it usually postpones rather than risk a floor defeat. That is especially likely when an extraordinary-session fallback is openly announced. The 2025 suspension did pass, but in extraordinary sessions and only after being cut back. My reference-class estimate is roughly 20-25% for passing on the specific target date.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - Santilli says he has the votes for media sanción (16 Nov).
  - The government says it has 10 of 19 committee signatures (14 Nov).
  - The bill has been watered down to a one-time suspension, which still counts, plus colectoras to win governors.
  - Several UCR governors are open to a suspension (La Nación, 14 Nov).
  - One count puts support at about 36, one short (15 Nov).
- For No:
  - Infobae counts about 31-32 votes (15 Nov).
  - PRO, whose 3 votes are needed, has hardened: Goerling called colectoras "un disparate", and PRO's board backed keeping the PASO.
  - Goerling doubts the dictamen will be signed if the text changes.
  - Bullrich, the LLA bloc leader, keeps saying the votes are not there.
  - Allies have not seen the new text.
  - Jaldo, Sáenz and Llaryora are opposed or raising demands.
  - December extraordinary sessions are an explicit fallback (Río Negro, 15 Nov).
  - Internal LLA conflict risks fracturing the bloc.

(e) No scenario: the dictamen slips, or is signed but the whip count stays at 34-36. The government pulls the item from the 26 Nov agenda and moves it to December extraordinary sessions, which is likely bundled with the budget. Alternatively, the text drifts toward optional primaries.
Yes scenario: the dictamen is signed on 17 Nov after colectoras are dropped to keep PRO on board. Governors trade budget concessions, UCR provincial senators plus Corroza, Royón and Vigo bring the total to 37 or more, and the bill passes in a long session on 26 Nov.

(f) I start from about 22%. I move down because several sequential hurdles must all clear, the independent counts are below 37, PRO is publicly resistant, and there is a comfortable December fallback. I give partial credit back for the government's push and the watered-down text. My final estimate is about 16%.

Probability: 16%

**(a) Time left and what must happen for Yes.** The outcome will be known in about 10 days, on 26-27 November 2026. For Yes, the Senate must hold a session on 26 November, or a continuation of it past midnight, and approve both en general and en particular a bill that suspends or eliminates the PASO for all 2027 national offices. That requires 37 votes. A bill making primaries optional, or suspending them only for some offices, resolves No.

**(b) Status quo.** The bill has been stalled since May. There is no dictamen, no formal call for the 26 November session, and the votes are disputed. If nothing changes, the answer is No.

**(c) Base rate.** The reference class is contested electoral bills in Argentina's Senate that lack a dictamen nine days before the last ordinary session, have unconfirmed votes and have an announced fallback to extraordinary sessions. These rarely pass on the target date, roughly 15-25%. The 2025 PASO suspension did pass, but in extraordinary sessions and after being cut back to a one-year suspension.

**(d) Strongest evidence.**

For Yes:
- On 14 November, Noticias Argentinas reported LLA claims 10 of the 19 committee signatures needed for the dictamen.
- On 16 November, Santilli was reported as saying he has the votes for media sanción.
- The bill has been narrowed to a one-time 2027 suspension, which would still count as Yes. Colectoras are being offered as a sweetener for governors.
- UCR governors Cornejo, Pullaro, Sadir, Zdero and Valdés are reportedly open to a suspension.

For No:
- On 15 November, Infobae counted about 31-32 votes and Análisis Digital about 36, both short of 37.
- The same day, PRO leader Goerling said he doesn't see the votes as certain, doubted the dictamen and called colectoras nonsense. PRO's executive board, with Macri present, backs keeping the PASO.
- Bullrich, who leads the LLA bloc, repeatedly says the votes aren't there.
- The internal fight over replacing Bullrich could fracture the bloc.
- The government has openly said December extraordinary sessions are its fallback.
- Governors Jaldo, Sáenz and Llaryora are opposed or have hardened their demands.
- Allied senators had not seen the new text as of 16 November.

**(e) Scenarios.**
- No: The text changes at the last minute, the dictamen slips or is signed without floor votes, and the Casa Rosada moves the bill to December extraordinary sessions. Alternatively, it is watered down to optional primaries.
- Yes: The dictamen is signed on 17 November, deals over budget transfers win over about 7 UCR senators plus provincial senators, PRO splits or abstains on a favourable count, and the bill passes on 26 November with about 37-39 votes.

**(f) From base rate to forecast.** I start at about 20%. The government's active push and the narrowing to a suspension, a version that has passed before, add a little. That is offset by the independent counts below 37, PRO's hardening, the uncertain dictamen, internal LLA conflict and an easy December fallback. The risk that a watered-down text resolves No pulls slightly lower. I end at about 15%.

Probability: 15%

(a) The outcome will be known in about 10 days, by 26-27 Nov 2026. For Yes, several things must all happen. Asuntos Constitucionales has to sign a dictamen, effectively on 17 Nov, so the bill can come to the floor without a two-thirds vote.
